findings.description: Using malloc/free and strdup in C++ is dangerous and error-prone.
The code assumes the file always contains 18 valid student records.
If the file is malformed or truncated, this can cause undefined behavior.
Use of strdup and raw pointers for names can lead to buffer overflows.
If an exception occurs or input fails, memory may not be freed.
Using a hardcoded file name can be a security risk.
No checks on the validity of exam scores or names.
